„Am Prellbock der Rangierwüste steht ein: "At the buffer stop in the shunting waste stands a hewer nobody ordered. He holds the last wagon fast, and in its coupling sits a rivet that once carried a whole train. I'll call him. You beat him without dodging. Whoever dodges is no buffer."
Holm schlägt mit dem Hemmschuh gegen die: Holm strikes the rail with the brake shoe. Far away a hammer answers, and then he stands there: the hewer, wider than any door. There is no dodging.
Holm bricht die Niete aus der Kupplung u: Holm breaks the rivet out of the coupling and puts it in your hand. "Load-bearing rivet. It holds what nobody ordered."
„Gleichfristblei. Das liegt als Gegengew: "Equal-deadline lead. It lies as a counterweight under the old turntable. I'll fetch it for you, but it costs: 9000 shillings and two lumps of shift gold, so the turntable doesn't tip."
Holm legt das Gold unter die Drehscheibe: Holm slides the gold under the turntable and pulls out the lead. "Weight for weight. That way it stays put."

„Fehlchargensalz? Mein Ofen macht jede W: "Faulty batch salt? My kiln makes a faulty batch every week. But the right one, the one that could have saved a city, that costs. 8000 shillings and three pieces of signal silver for the grate."
Senta kratzt einen grauen Belag aus dem: Senta scrapes a grey crust out of the kiln and wraps it in brown paper. "Faulty batch salt. Don't breathe it in."
„Kalklicht ist das hellste Licht, das ei: "Limelight is the brightest light a person can make. I'll light a wick in it, and that brings the threshold hound in from the shunting waste. Beat it while the wick burns, without healing. Then the wick will have seen something it never forgets."
Senta hält den Docht ins Kalklicht. Es w: Senta holds the wick into the limelight. It grows so bright you shut your eyes, and when you open them the threshold hound stands before you, white with lime. You cannot heal in this light.
Senta löscht den Docht zwischen zwei Fin: Senta pinches out the wick and hands it to you. "Witness wick. It saw you fight."
„Zwischen dem letzten Signal und dem ers: "Between the last signal and the first train there's a second that belongs to no one. I've diverted one. 9000 shillings and a lump of shift gold, for the pointsmen who saw nothing."
Der Streckenläufer klappt die Uhr auf, z: The Track Walker flips open his watch, draws something out from between two hands and puts it in yours. "Between-second. Delivered on time."
„Im Klopfbruch hängt ein Signaldraht, de: "In the knocking quarry hangs a signal wire that leads nowhere anymore. The hewer got tangled in it and winds up everything that's missing. I pull the wire, he comes. You beat him without any healing, or he winds you up too."
Der Streckenläufer zieht am Draht. Irgen: The Track Walker pulls the wire. Somewhere in the quarry something clinks, and the hewer comes, the wire wound round his arms like a spool. You cannot heal here.
Der Streckenläufer wickelt den Draht von: The Track Walker unwinds the wire from a small spool and hands it to you. "Gap spool. What is missing, it holds fast."
„Der Vielrufer in der Rufschlucht hat al: "The Many-Caller in the calling gorge has eaten every voice of the shift. I'll sing him here. But when he comes you'll hear nothing, no call, no warning. Beat him deaf and he'll give up a pause."
Jory singt einen Ton, der zu tief für ei: Jory sings a note too deep for a human. The gorge answers with a hundred voices, and then it goes quiet. The Many-Caller is here, and you hear nothing anymore.
Jory hält ein leeres Fläschchen an die L: Jory holds an empty vial to the fallen one's lips and corks it. "Breathing pause. The last one he had."
„Rückseitenwachs? Damit versiegeln sie d: "Backside wax? They seal the cylinders with it, the ones that hold the voices of the dead. A face stays on the back. 8500 shillings and a lump of shift gold. I don't sing for free."
Jory schabt das Wachs von einer alten Wa: Jory scrapes the wax off an old cylinder. Pressed into the back is a face that looks at you. "Backside wax. Wear it however you like."
„Unter dem Endbahnhof steht Grundwasser,: "Under the terminus there's groundwater, and the Undershift lies in it. It swallowed a name, deep down. I'll call it up. You drink moor water every round, or the water lets you go. Bring enough."
Wenna legt die Hand auf die Schranke und: Wenna lays her hand on the barrier and whispers a name. The cobbles turn wet, then the Undershift rises from the groundwater. You must drink moor water every round.
Wenna fischt ein schlammiges Täfelchen a: Wenna fishes a muddy tablet out of the puddle. "Layer name. It's yours now. Take good care of it."
„Ich mache die Schranke auf und zu, für: "I open and close the barrier for anyone who wants through. Some leave a key for it. One of them has a toll bit that opens any border. 9000 shillings. That's the fare for the whole line."
Wenna holt einen Schlüssel aus dem Schra: Wenna fetches a key from the barrier hut and puts it in your hand. "Toll bit. Don't open anything with it that should stay shut."
